title: Remembering the Second World War
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:52Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point covers the aftermath of the First World War in Europe (empires, debt, unstable states), while the new point is about how Australia remembers the Second World War through Anzac Day, memorials, Kokoda and debates over national identity, so no bank point teaches the same idea.

draft.title: Remembering the Second World War
card: Anzac Day, held on 25 April, began by remembering the First World War. It now honours Australians who served in all wars, including the Second World War.
Memorials, such as the Australian War Memorial in Canberra and local war memorials, keep the names and stories of those who served in public view.
Kokoda in Papua New Guinea, where Australians fought in 1942, has become a place of pilgrimage. Many Australians now walk the Kokoda Track to honour those who fought there.
Historians debate what the war means for Australian identity. They disagree about which events matter most and what they say about the nation.
draft.remember: Days, memorials and places keep the war remembered, but its meaning is still debated.

a.q: What does it mean to call Kokoda a place of pilgrimage?
opts: Many Australians travel there to honour those who fought
Australians are required to visit it as part of school
It is where Anzac Day is held each year
It is the site of the Australian War Memorial
a.why: A pilgrimage is a journey made to honour a place of meaning, and many Australians walk the Kokoda Track. The Australian War Memorial is in Canberra, not Kokoda.
a.clue: A pilgrimage is a journey with meaning.

b.q: Two historians disagree about what the Second World War shows about Australian identity. What does this tell us?
opts: The war's meaning is open to different views
One historian must have the facts wrong
The war is not remembered in Australia
Anzac Day has stopped being observed
b.why: Historians can agree on events yet interpret their meaning differently, so debate is normal. Disagreeing about meaning does not mean one has the facts wrong.
b.clue: Disagreement can be about meaning, not facts.

a.best: Many Australians travel there to honour those who fought

b.best: The war's meaning is open to different views

check.summary: No problems found. The facts about Anzac Day, the Australian War Memorial and Kokoda are accurate, each question has one clearly right answer, and the explanations match the card.
